items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: when I left Benny Goodman, I vowed that I would never work again for another bandleader and I never have

ctx.x: earlier in the tapes, it was no different from being in a factory because you cannot play music all day long and love it. It was like pulling teeth, you know.

So we, who thought we were going to escape into an easy life, found that we might have picked the most difficult life we could. But I am very happy that I got into it, because now I have things pretty much my own way. I have stopped -- when I left Benny Goodman, I vowed that I would never work again for another bandleader and I never have. I went out as a soloist and there were many lean years, and I just managed to survive and then I finally, I think the last band I played with, I am sure it was the last band I…

I stayed with that thing for six years, because in that band, I was -- the band was built around ten soloists in the beginning and then went to nine and later to seven, and we had all the freedom we wanted. We could play -- I was there because I was a soloist. I could do anything I wanted. We made plenty of money. We had a very good way of life and we didn't work hard. There was a lot of traveling and a lot of sleep lost different days, but I -- we came to Europe a couple of times and I got a picture of London…
